reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical Design - Part 1: General Rules
chapter_title: Annex C (informative): Sample procedures to determine earth pressures

sections.title: Annex C.1: Limit values of earth pressure
sections.summary: Gives the basic active/passive earth-pressure formulas: total stress normal to a vertical wall at depth z is sigma_a(z) = Ka*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u - c*Kac (active, Eq. C.1) or sigma_p(z) = Kp*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u + c*Kpc (passive, Eq. C.2), with Kac = 2*sqrt[Ka*(1+a/c)] capped at 2.56*sqrt(Ka) and Kpc = 2*sqrt[Kp*(1+a/c)] capped at 2.56*sqrt(Kp). Ka/Kp come from design charts (Figures C.1.1-C.1.4 for Ka, C.2.1-C.2.4 for Kp, by delta/phi' ratio and slope) or the Annex C.2 analytical procedure; for undrained soil Ka=Kp=1 and c=cu.
sections.body: The limit values of earth pressure on a vertical wall, caused by soil of weight density gamma, uniform vertical surface load q, angle of shearing resistance phi, and cohesion c, are calculated for the active limit state as sigma_a(z) = Ka*[integral of gamma dz from ground surface to depth z, plus q, minus u] + u - c*Kac (Eq. C.1), where Kac = 2*sqrt[Ka*(1+a/c)], limited to 2.56*sqrt(Ka). For the passive limit state, sigma_p(z) = Kp*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u + c*Kpc (Eq. C.2), with the integration likewise taken from the ground surface to depth z, where Kpc = 2*sqrt[Kp*(1+a/c)], limited to 2.56*sqrt(Kp). Symbols: a is the adhesion between ground and wall; c is the cohesion; Ka/Kp are the coefficients of effective horizontal active/passive earth pressure; q is the vertical surface load; z is distance down the wall face; beta is the slope angle of the ground behind the wall (positive rising away from the wall); delta is the angle of shearing resistance between ground and wall (wall friction angle); gamma is the total weight density of the retained ground; sigma_a(z)/sigma_p(z) are the total stresses normal to the wall at depth z. For drained soil, Ka and Kp are functions of the angle of shearing resistance phi' and the effective cohesion c'; for undrained soil, Ka = Kp = 1 and c = cu (the undrained shear strength). Values of the effective earth-pressure coefficients may be taken from Figures C.1.1 to C.1.4 for Ka (horizontal retained surface, and inclined surface at delta/phi' = 0, 0.66, and 1.0) and Figures C.2.1 to C.2.4 for Kp (same delta/phi' groupings), each plotted against phi' with beta as a curve parameter; alternatively the analytical procedure of C.2 may be used. In layered soils, K should normally be determined from the shear strength parameters at depth z only, independent of values at other depths.
key_points: Active pressure: sigma_a(z) = Ka*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u - c*Kac (Eq. C.1)
Passive pressure: sigma_p(z) = Kp*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u + c*Kpc (Eq. C.2)
Kac = 2*sqrt[Ka*(1+a/c)], limited to 2.56*sqrt(Ka); Kpc = 2*sqrt[Kp*(1+a/c)], limited to 2.56*sqrt(Kp) -- both IMPLEMENTED as cohesion_earth_pressure_coefficient
Ka from Figures C.1.1-C.1.4, Kp from Figures C.2.1-C.2.4, by delta/phi' ratio (0, 0.66, 1.0) and slope beta
Undrained soil: Ka = Kp = 1 and c = cu
In layered soils, K uses the shear strength parameters AT depth z only, not other depths
Eq. C.1/C.2 themselves ARE implemented as active_earth_pressure / passive_earth_pressure

equations.description: Total active earth pressure normal to the wall at depth z: sigma_a(z) = Ka*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u - c*Kac.
Total passive earth pressure normal to the wall at depth z: sigma_p(z) = Kp*[integral(gamma dz) + q - u] + u + c*Kpc.

sections.title: Annex C.2: Analytical procedure for obtaining limiting active and passive earth pressures
sections.summary: An analytical procedure, with certain approximations, that may be used in all cases as an alternative to the Figures C.1/C.2 charts. Stated for passive pressure with phi, c, delta, a positive; for active pressure the same algorithm with these negative and beta0 = beta. cos(2mt + phi + beta0) = -sin(beta0)/sin(phi) (C.3); cos(2mw + phi + delta) = sin(delta)/sin(phi) (C.4); v = mt + beta - mw - theta (C.5); Kn = [1 + sin(phi) sin(2mw + phi)]/[1 - sin(phi) sin(2mt + phi)] exp(2v tan(phi)) (C.6); Kq = Kn cos^2(beta) (C.7); Kc = (Kn - 1) cot(phi) (C.8); Kgamma = Kn cos(beta) cos(beta - theta) (C.9, safe side); phi = 0 limit values and Kgamma (C.10).
sections.body: (1) The following procedure, which includes certain approximations, may be used in all cases. (2) The procedure is stated for passive pressures with the strength parameters (phi, c, delta, a) inserted as positive values, see Figure C.3. (3) For active pressures the same algorithm is used, with the following changes: the strength parameters phi, c, delta and a are inserted as negative values; the value of the angle of incidence of the equivalent surface load beta0 is beta, mainly because of the approximations used for Kgamma. (4) Symbols: a = adhesion between wall and ground; c = cohesion; Kc = coefficient for cohesion; Kn = coefficient for normal loading on the surface; Kq = coefficient for vertical loading; Kgamma = coefficient for the soil weight; mt = angle from the soil surface direction, pointing away from the wall, to the tangent direction of the intersecting slip line that bounds the moving soil mass, pointing out from the soil surface; mw = angle from the wall normal to the tangent direction at the wall of the exterior slip line, positive when the tangent points upwards behind the wall; beta = angle from the horizontal to the soil surface direction, positive when the soil surface rises away from the wall; delta = angle of wall friction, with sign convention 'as defined in Figure C.4' when computing passive resistance (as printed; the printed Figure C.4 is the mobilisation curve of C.3, and delta > 0 is drawn in Figure C.3 a)); phi = angle of shearing resistance; theta = angle between the vertical and the wall direction, positive when the soil overhangs the wall; v = tangent rotation along the exterior slip line, positive when the soil mass above this slip line is of a convex shape; q = general uniform surcharge pressure per unit area of the actual surface; p = vertical uniform surcharge pressure per unit area in a horizontal projection. (5) The interface parameters delta and a must be chosen so that a/c = tan(delta)/tan(phi). (6) The boundary condition at the soil surface involves beta0, the angle of incidence of an equivalent surface load, defined from the vectorial sum of the actual distributed surface loading q (per unit of surface area, uniform but not necessarily vertical) and c*cot(phi) acting as normal load. beta0 is positive when the tangential component of q points toward the wall while the normal component is directed toward the soil. If c = 0 while the surface load is vertical or zero, and for active pressures generally, beta0 = beta. (7) The angle mt is determined by the boundary condition at the soil surface: cos(2mt + phi + beta0) = -sin(beta0)/sin(phi) (Eq. C.3). (8) The boundary condition at the wall determines mw by cos(2mw + phi + delta) = sin(delta)/sin(phi) (Eq. C.4); mw is negative for passive pressures (phi > 0) if the ratio sin(delta)/sin(phi) is sufficiently large. (9) The total tangent rotation along the exterior slip line of the moving soil mass is determined by the angle v = mt + beta - mw - theta (Eq. C.5). (10) The coefficient Kn for normal loading on the surface (the normal earth pressure on the wall from a unit pressure normal to the surface), with v in radians: Kn = [1 + sin(phi)*sin(2mw + phi)]/[1 - sin(phi)*sin(2mt + phi)] * exp(2v*tan(phi)) (Eq. C.6). (11) The coefficient for a vertical loading on the surface (force per unit of horizontal area projection) is Kq = Kn*cos^2(beta) (Eq. C.7), and the coefficient for the cohesion term is Kc = (Kn - 1)*cot(phi) (Eq. C.8). (12) For the soil weight an approximate expression is Kgamma = Kn*cos(beta)*cos(beta - theta) (Eq. C.9). This expression is on the safe side; while the error is unimportant for active pressures it may be considerable for passive pressures with positive values of beta. For phi = 0 the following limit values are found: cos 2mt = -(p/c)*sin(beta)*cos(beta); cos 2mw = a/c; Kq = cos^2(beta); Kc = 2v + sin 2mt + sin 2mw (with v in radians); while for Kgamma (phi = 0) a better approximation is Kgamma = cos(theta) + sin(beta)*cos(mw)/sin(mt) (Eq. C.10). (13) Both for passive and active pressures, the procedure assumes the angle of convexity to be positive (v >= 0). (14) If this condition is not (even approximately) fulfilled, e.g. for a smooth wall and a sufficiently sloping soil surface when beta and phi have opposite signs, it may be necessary to consider using other methods. This may also be the case when irregular surface loads are considered. In this package Eq. C.4 is implemented as mobilised_wall_angle_mw and Eq. C.9 as weight_density_coefficient (Kn supplied by the caller); Eqs. C.3, C.5 to C.8 and C.10 are not implemented as functions.
key_points: May be used in all cases; stated for passive pressure with phi, c, delta, a positive; active pressure uses the same algorithm with these negative and beta0 = beta
The interface parameters must be chosen so that a/c = tan(delta)/tan(phi)
Eq. C.3: cos(2mt + phi + beta0) = -sin(beta0)/sin(phi); Eq. C.4: cos(2mw + phi + delta) = sin(delta)/sin(phi) (implemented as mobilised_wall_angle_mw)
Eq. C.5: v = mt + beta - mw - theta; Eq. C.6: Kn = [1 + sin(phi) sin(2mw + phi)]/[1 - sin(phi) sin(2mt + phi)] exp(2v tan(phi)), v in radians
Eq. C.7: Kq = Kn cos^2(beta); Eq. C.8: Kc = (Kn - 1) cot(phi)
Eq. C.9: Kgamma = Kn cos(beta) cos(beta - theta), on the safe side; the error may be considerable for passive pressures with positive beta (implemented as weight_density_coefficient)
phi = 0: cos 2mt = -(p/c) sin(beta) cos(beta); cos 2mw = a/c; Kq = cos^2(beta); Kc = 2v + sin 2mt + sin 2mw; Kgamma = cos(theta) + sin(beta) cos(mw)/sin(mt) (Eq. C.10)
The procedure assumes v >= 0; if not even approximately fulfilled, or with irregular surface loads, it may be necessary to consider using other methods

equations.description: Boundary condition at the soil surface determining mt: cos(2mt + phi + beta0) = -sin(beta0)/sin(phi).
Boundary condition at the wall determining angle mw: cos(2*mw+phi+delta) = sin(delta)/sin(phi).
Total tangent rotation along the exterior slip line: v = mt + beta - mw - theta.
Coefficient for normal loading on the surface: Kn = [1 + sin(phi)*sin(2mw + phi)]/[1 - sin(phi)*sin(2mt + phi)] * exp(2v*tan(phi)), v in radians.
Coefficient for vertical loading on the surface (per unit of horizontal projection): Kq = Kn*cos^2(beta).
Coefficient for the cohesion term: Kc = (Kn - 1)*cot(phi).
Approximate soil-weight coefficient Kgamma = Kn*cos(beta)*cos(beta-theta); safe-sided, given Kn.

For phi = 0, a better approximation for the soil-weight coefficient: Kgamma = cos(theta) + sin(beta)*cos(mw)/sin(mt). The other phi = 0 limit values (unnumbered): cos 2mt = -(p/c) sin(beta) cos(beta); cos 2mw = a/c; Kq = cos^2(beta); Kc = 2v + sin 2mt + sin 2mw.

sections.title: Annex C.3: Movements to mobilise earth pressures
sections.summary: Gives approximate wall-displacement ratios needed to fully mobilise active (Table C.1, ratio va/h) or passive (Table C.2, ratio vp/h) earth pressure in drained, non-cohesive soil with a horizontal ground surface and Ko<1, by mode of wall movement and soil density (loose/dense). Active pressure varies linearly with displacement between rest and limit states; passive mobilisation follows the nonlinear curve of Figure C.4 (values from Table C.2, including the v/h for half the limiting passive pressure).
sections.body: The relationship between earth pressure and wall movement should be considered for both active and passive situations; the magnitude of movement needed depends on the mode of wall movement, the initial earth pressure, and the soil density. Table C.1 gives approximate ratios va/h (wall motion to mobilise active earth pressure, over wall height h) for a vertical wall with drained, non-cohesive soil and a horizontal ground surface, assuming an initial stress state with Ko<1, by mode of wall movement (translation, rotation about the top or base, etc.) and by loose vs. dense soil (ranging roughly 0.05% to 1.0% of h depending on mode and density). Table C.2 gives approximate ratios vp/h (wall displacement to mobilise passive earth pressure) for the same soil/wall conditions, with values in brackets giving the v/h ratio for half the limiting passive pressure (ranging roughly 3% to 25% of h). Intermediate values of effective active earth pressure between the at-rest state and the limit state may be obtained by linear interpolation. For passive situations, intermediate values may be interpolated from Table C.2 using the nonlinear mobilisation curve of general form shown in Figure C.4 (effective passive pressure, normalised to Ko and to the limiting passive value, plotted against normalised wall displacement v/vp).
key_points: Table C.1: ratio va/h to mobilise ACTIVE earth pressure, by wall-movement mode and soil density (loose/dense), drained non-cohesive soil, Ko<1
Table C.2: ratio vp/h (and v/h for 0.5*passive pressure, in brackets) to mobilise PASSIVE earth pressure, same conditions
Table C.2 gives vp/h of 3 to 25 %, Table C.1 va/h of 0.05 to 1.0 %
Active pressure between rest and limit states: linear interpolation with displacement
Passive pressure mobilisation follows the nonlinear curve of Figure C.4, referenced to Table C.2 values
